page: OVHcloud b3-32 is a general-purpose virtual instance deployed on KVM hypervisor architecture. The instance is powered by an AMD EPYC x86_64 processor clocked at 2.3 GHz, delivering 8 dedicated vCPUs with 1 thread per physical core. The hardware configuration integrates 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. Memory capacity is configured at 32.0 GB of RAM, preserving a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory allocation of 4.0 GB per core. The server includes 200 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps. Accelerated computing via dedicated GPUs is not present on this instance type.

Benchmark results show balanced compute and memory throughput. Single-core processing is highlighted by a stress-ng score of 3077.97, placing it in the top 25 percent tier, alongside an average Geekbench single-core result of 1858.0. Multi-core performance aligns with expected eight-thread capacity, logging 24559.94 in stress-ng and 8885.0 in Geekbench multi-core tests. Memory throughput demonstrates notable performance in large-block uncached write bandwidth at 96.92 GB/sec and a PassMark memory score of 2793.86, both registering in the top 25 percent benchmark segment, complemented by 133.5 GB/sec uncached read bandwidth.

Workload execution profiles show steady throughput across standard service tasks, logging 19.62 million operations per second in Redis SET tests and 8.61 GB/sec in static web serving benchmarks. Small-model LLM generation (135M) achieves 290.79 tokens per second, though medium-scale 7B inference operates within average bands at 19.81 tokens per second. The presence of bundled local NVMe storage combined with a standard 1:4 memory profile makes the instance cost-efficient for applications requiring consistent dedicated vCPU performance without overpaying for specialized compute or massive memory overhead.

Tradeoffs for the b3-32 center around instruction support and I/O ceilings. The AMD processor features standard AVX, AES-NI, and SHA extensions, but lacks AVX-512 and AMX instruction sets, which limits optimization for vector-heavy and specialized matrix tasks. Furthermore, the 2 Gbps baseline network interface and 200 GB local NVMe storage bound high-throughput distributed applications. The configuration is technically matched for web application hosting, build systems, CI/CD pipelines, caching tiers, and medium-scale database workloads.
description: OVHcloud b3-32 is a general-purpose KVM virtual instance powered by an AMD EPYC x86_64 processor clocked at 2.3 GHz. The configuration provides 8 dedicated physical cores and 8 vCPUs without multithreading, coupled with 32.0 GB of RAM, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB per core ratio. Storage is bundled with a local 200 GB NVMe SSD, complemented by a 2 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. The system achieves strong single-core stress-ng performance and top-quartile uncached memory write throughput of 96.92 GB/sec alongside a PassMark memory score of 2793.86. Multi-core execution and network serving sustain steady middle-tier benchmark metrics, such as 19.62 million Redis SET operations per second. Lacking AVX-512 and hardware GPUs, the b3-32 provides predictable resource density suited for web application serving, continuous integration environments, caching, and mid-tier transactional databases.
